タイルを1枚ずつつなげて地図を広げ、できあがった都市や道に置いた自分のコマ（ミー: Players add tiles one at a time to grow a shared map, and score with the pieces (meeples) they place on the cities and roads they build. This page explains, with diagrams, all the rules you need to play.
<span class=\"no\">1</span>手番にやること: 1What you do on your turn
<b>タイルを1枚引いて置く。</b>すでにあるタイルの隣に、辺の絵がつながるよ: Draw a tile and place it. Put it next to a tile already on the table so that the edges match.
<b>ミープルを置いてもよい。</b>今置いたタイルの上の都市・道・修道院・草原: You may place a meeple. You can put one of your meeples on one city, road, monastery or field on the tile you just placed. You don't have to.
<b>完成したら得点。</b>都市・道・修道院が完成したら、そこにミープルを置い: Score what is completed. When a city, road or monastery is completed, the player with meeples on it scores, and the meeples go back to their owners.
山札がなくなったらゲーム終了です。最後に、完成していないものと草原の点を数え、合: The game ends when the tiles run out. Then you score unfinished features and fields, and the player with the most points wins.
<span class=\"k\">例</span>最初のタイルの右に、<spa: ExampleThe tile in the yellow frame was placed to the right of the start tile. Road meets road and field meets field. A city edge can only touch a city edge, and a road only a road. You may rotate the tile any way you like.
どこにも置けないタイルを引いたら、そのタイルは使わずに箱へ戻し、もう1枚引きます: If you draw a tile that fits nowhere, put it back in the box unused and draw another.
ミープルは1人7個。置けるのは<b>今置いたタイルの上だけ</b>です。: Each player has 7 meeples. You can only place one on the tile you just placed.
つながった都市や道に<b>すでに誰かのミープルがいたら、そこには置けません</b: If a connected city or road already has a meeple on it, you can't place there (even if it is your own).
別々に置いた都市があとでつながって、1つの都市に複数のミープルがいることになるの: Two separately claimed cities may later join, leaving several meeples in one city. Then the player with the most meeples scores; if tied, all tied players score in full.
置いたミープルは、その場所が完成するまで戻ってきません。草原のミープル（農民）は: A meeple stays put until its feature is completed. Meeples in fields (farmers) never come back before the end.
周りの8マスが全部埋まったら9点: 9 when all 8 surrounding squares are filled
<span class=\"k\">例</span><span class=\": ExampleRed has a meeple in a city with a shield. Placing a city tile in the yellow frame closes the 3-tile city. 3 tiles × 2 + 1 shield × 2 = 8 points, and the meeple comes back.
<span class=\"k\">例</span>道は、十字路・修道院・都市な: ExampleA road is complete when both ends stop at a crossing, monastery, city and so on. Red's road ends at a crossing on the left; placing another crossing in the yellow frame completes it. 3 tiles, 3 points.
<span class=\"k\">例</span><span class=\": Example5 of the 8 squares around Red's monastery (yellow frame) are filled. Filling all of them gives 9 points; if the game ends now, it scores 1 for the monastery + 5 squares = 6 points.

ExampleBlue has a meeple in the field on the upper side of the tile in the yellow frame (a meeple in a field is called a farmer). This field touches the city completed a moment ago, so it scores 3 points at the end. If the city were unfinished, it would score 0.
最後のタイルを置いて得点したら終了です。盤上に残っているミープルについて、上の表: The game ends once the last tile is placed and scored. For each meeple still on the board, add the "at the end" points from the table above. The player with the highest total wins.
まずは<b>小さな都市を作って閉じる</b>のがいちばん確実に点になります。: Building small cities and closing them is the surest way to score at first.
ミープルは7個しかありません。<b>なかなか完成しない長い道</b>に置くと、し: You only have 7 meeples. Put one on a long road that is slow to finish and it won't come back for a while.
迷ったら、<b>今すぐ完成させられるもの</b>がないか探しましょう。点が入り、: When in doubt, look for something you can complete right now. You score, and your meeple comes back.

このページのルールについて: About the rules on this page
基本セット（72枚）の現行ルールです。農民は完成した都市1つにつき3点で数えます: These are the current rules of the base game (72 tiles). Farmers score 3 points per completed city (older editions counted differently). The diagrams are real positions played with this project's rules engine, and the points in the text are checked against the engine's scoring (scripts/build_rules_page.py). The examples assume two players, but 2–5 players use the same rules.
